ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a conjugated enol-iminium transition-state structure with curved arrows; on the left is a benzene ring, and the benzene ring is connected to a positively charged nitrogen atom bearing hydrogen. The nitrogen atom forms an imine double bond with the carbon on the right, and the carbon on the right is also connected to R1. This carbon is then connected to the adjacent alkene carbon, and the adjacent carbon continues to form a double bond with the enol carbon above bearing OH; this enol carbon bearing OH is also connected to R2. The curved arrows in the figure are ignored according to the prompt. Reasoning: Represent both R2 and R1 with the wildcard atom *; write the enol carbon bearing OH as *C(O)=, and after the middle double bond connect to the subsequent carbon according to the stereochemical direction shown in the figure, using =C\C(*)=; write the protonated nitrogen as [NH+], and it then connects to phenyl c1ccccc1, retaining the slash direction shown in the figure as /c1ccccc1. Therefore the SMILES is *C(O)=C\C(*)=[NH+]/c1ccccc1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a conjugated enol-iminium transition-state structure: R2 is attached to the enol carbon bearing OH, this carbon is double-bonded to the next carbon, which is connected to a carbon bearing R1 and double-bonded to a protonated N; the N is also bonded to H and to a phenyl ring. Then use the text instruction to ignore all curved arrows. Replace R2 and R1 by wildcard atoms, encode the phenyl as 'c1ccccc1' attached to '[NH+]', and write the chain with the displayed slash/backslash stereochemistry to obtain '*C(O)=C\C(*)=[NH+]/c1ccccc1'.
